Subject: Discovery recap & proposed acceptance plan for Medisys pilot

Hi Tom / Marta —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written recap and a proposed next-step plan so we can get the pilot moving without losing momentum. Please confirm owners and any edits to the success criteria below.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Goal: validate Redwood inference latency and throughput against Medisys clinical-assistant prompts and integration with your API gateway.
- Primary constraints: on-prem-like data residency (VPC peering), audit logs, and predictable 99th percentile latency under mixed prompt lengths.

Proposed pilot outline (4 weeks):
1) Integration (2 business weeks): config, test harness, and basic traffic routing — target March 16–27.
2) Validation (1 week): run representative traffic with NVMe-backed KV cache enabled for prefix patterns — target March 30–April 3.
3) Readout + decision (Executive 30-min): week of April 6 — proposed March 30 or April 6 as options.

Proposed acceptance criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: 99th percentile < 400 ms for clinical prompt set A (50–250 tokens).
- Quality: BLEU-like reranking pass rate >= 88% on curated eval set (we will run the set and share raw results).
- Throughput: sustain 120 req/min average with <=2% error rate.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 alignment & audit logs available for the pilot window.

Ownership (please confirm or update):
- Medisys: Tom Ellis (Platform lead) — integration owner; Marta Ruiz (Product) — success criteria owner
- Redwood: Aditya Rao (AE) — program lead; Priyom Das (SE) — technical lead; Neha Kapoor (CS) — validation & runbook owner

Attachments I just uploaded: medisys_trial_success_criteria.xlsx (editable scorecard). I can also add a more detailed runbook if you want — Priyom has a draft.

Asks / immediate next steps:
- Can you confirm owners and accept or adjust the acceptance criteria above by EOD Thursday, Mar 12?
- Confirm whether SOC2 summary (attached) is sufficient for your procurement team or whether we should route an NDA/procurement packet first.
- Pick preferred readout windows (Mar 30, Apr 6) — we will hold both tentatively until you confirm.

If that looks good I’ll get Priyom to publish a runbook and calendar invites for the integration kickoff.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147

Aditya —

Thanks for the clear recap. Overall this aligns with our expectations. A couple of quick edits from our side: 
- Throughput target: can we set the target to sustain 100 req/min average (not 120) but require tail stability (99th) under test traffic? Our production patterns are bursty and the tail behavior is more important for us.
- Quality: we prefer a practical pass metric that uses our clinical-fidelity rubric — if Redwood can map the BLEU-like metric to our rubric that’s great.
- Timeline: two-week integration sounds right but we will need a short blackout window for our infra refresh on Mar 18; can the integration window be Mar 16–20 and then resume Mar 23–27?

Procurement note: our procurement lead asked for a SOC2 summary and a sketch of data retention/audit log retention — the attached SOC2 summary helps. Please also confirm encryption-at-rest and KMS options.

I can confirm owners as listed — Marta and I will own internal coordination. We prefer the executive review on Mar 30 morning if possible.

—Tom
Tom Ellis
Platform Engineering Lead, Medisys
tom.ellis@medisys.com | +1 213-555-1288

Tom / team —

Thanks, quick technical clarifications and a proposed runbook. I’ll own the integration work with Tom’s platform team. High level:

Runbook highlights (draft):
- Pre-kickoff (by Mar 13): exchange API endpoints, sample prompt corpus, and service account keys.
- Integration week 1 (Mar 16–20): VPC peering test, sample traffic (non-prod) for KV/cache tuning, basic auth and logging verification.
- Infra refresh blackout (Mar 18): we’ll pause any non-critical config changes; I’ll coordinate a low-impact test plan for that day.
- Integration week 2 (Mar 23–27): end-to-end tests, production-like load window (staged), and data capture for quality review.
- Validation (Mar 30–Apr 3): scoring run, side-by-side result sampling, and incident window for fixes.

Config notes:
- We will enable prefix KV caching for reusable clinical prompts — this typically reduces token work and improves tail latency; we will provide a config snippet.
- Logging: we will stream request/response metadata to your S3-compatible bucket for the trial window; PII will be redacted per mutual agreement.

Deliverables I’ll upload to the runbook drive: rdw_trial_runbook_v1.xlsx and a short JIT checklist.

Proposed exec readout date: Mar 30, 10:00–10:30 PT. If that slot works for Medisys we’ll lock it and invite relevant execs + legal/procurement.

If you want I can also add an automated scorecard we’ll fill after validation to show pass/fail per criterion.

—Priyom
